scenario: AITA for not believing my coworker about “chronic pain”? | I have a coworker in his mid 30s who claims to suffer from chronic pain. Frankly, I think it’s a load of crap. He claims it’s from a botched surgery. Somehow he’s been granted FMLA. There are plenty of other days though when he’s walking around just fine, even talking walks in the park across from our office or standing around at a coworker’s desk laughing while they talk. I’ve made comments like “Gee, you look like you’re really hurting!” on those days and he just says “I’m having a good day. They happen.” Recently he started using a cane as a prop, which is when I confronted him. There’s no way it’s legitimate need. I asked him just how bad his surgery was that now he needs a cane, adding that it was taking the act a bit too far. He pulled up his shirt and revealed a dinky little 4” scar near his waist. I said laughed and said “That’s why you’re stumbling around?” He replied “This is the outside. I hope you get to feel what I feel, asshole.” Then he shuffled away with his cane and next thing I know I’m getting talked to by our boss about how I’m treating Mr. Pain and that it’s inappropriate. When I told my boss I knew he was faking, he told me “his doctors know more than you” and that if I ever voiced doubt about the coworker in the office again, I’d be looking for a new job.
